goal: Give Codex, Hermes, and media Adapters one durable Harness settlement Interface so execution, delivery, Artifact, and task lifecycle cannot drift apart across callback replay or process restart.

acceptance_criteria.description: begin is idempotent and every migrated Codex, Hermes, and media attempt has a durable Harness execution before executor work starts.
settle records one durable settlement per execution, rejects conflicting replay, and returns the same receipt after process restart.
A completed task requires confirmed or not-required delivery evidence; runtime-owned delivery may only close an attempt into review_required or blocked.
Successful media settlement requires an Artifact and atomically records Artifact lineage with the execution outcome and pending settlement record.
reconcile applies a durable pending task transition after a simulated crash without duplicating the Artifact or lifecycle event.
Codex and Hermes Adapters persist request and result digests, usage, provenance, and delivery references without persisting complete prompts or complete answers in settlement metadata.
Router media, GPT Image, Dreamina, Codex, and Hermes production Adapters use the shared Executor Settlement Interface rather than directly pairing execution and Harness task terminal writes.
Harness runtime startup exposes one shared Executor Settlement instance and reconciles durable pending settlements without granting scheduling ownership to any executor.

non_goals: Do not make Harness the Router or scheduler.
Do not move card rendering or message delivery into Harness.
Do not persist complete Codex prompts or complete Codex/Hermes answers.
Do not merge executor invocation implementations.
Do not trigger Obsidian publication or long-term distillation in this phase.
